detail.longDescription: I am working on a vehicle inspection workflow where users upload photos of a car from different angles. I want to use computer vision to identify visible issues such as dents, scratches, cracked lights, and damaged body panels. The main challenge is that inspection photos can have different lighting conditions, camera angles, image quality, and backgrounds. I am considering an object-detection or image-classification approach, but I am unsure which method would be more appropriate for detecting different types of vehicle damage. What computer-vision approach would you recommend for this type of inspection system? Should I train a custom object-detection model using labeled vehicle-damage images, or would image classification combined with segmentation be more suitable? I am particularly interested in recommendations for preparing the training dataset, handling different lighting and angles, and evaluating the model's accuracy.
